scene: Inferno XXV — serpent-human fusion, exchange and identity tracking
story: Vanni Fucci makes an obscene gesture toward heaven and flees while serpents pursue; a serpent coils around his neck.
The centaur Cacus appears, bearing snakes and a fire-breathing dragon, and races after the blaspheming thief.
Dante watches Agnello Brunelleschi embraced by a six-footed serpent identified with Cianfa Donati; their shapes fuse into a single indistinct composite.
A second serpent attacks Buoso Donati. Smoke accompanies a reciprocal transformation: the man takes reptilian form while the serpent becomes human.
Francesco Cavalcanti, called Guercio, is associated with that second serpent; the transformations make tracking the participants harder, not optional.
Puccio Sciancato remains in human shape as a contrast to those transformed.
Dante and Virgil proceed, maintaining the order of observed transformations and distinguishing Cianfa, Agnello, Buoso, Francesco and Puccio.
